overview: Taihoku despatch reports Japan Air Transport's twin-engine 'ENVOY' crashed nearing Giran from Taito on June 24, 1938, killing the pilot and four Japanese passengers, tentatively blamed on a wind gust, called Japan's worst commercial air disaster after two earlier Fukuoka crashes.

subfiles.title: Despatch on the fatal Japan Air Transport crash at Giran
subfiles.from: William E. Young, American Vice Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington, D.C.
subfiles.about: Reports the June 24, 1938 crash of a Japan Air Transport Company passenger aircraft at Giran, Taiwan, which killed the pilot and four passengers.
subfiles.summary: Despatch: a Japan Air Transport twin-engine plane crashed near Giran returning from Taito, killing the pilot and four Japanese passengers; Young calls it Japan's worst commercial aviation disaster, suspecting a wind gust and comparing it to earlier Fukuoka crashes.

interest: Shows an early Japanese commercial-aviation fatal crash in Taiwan, reported through the consular network.
